stem: A batch feels dry at the surface, but sealed representative samples later show rising internal humidity. Which explanation best fits drying science?
choices: Internal moisture was still redistributing, so the initial endpoint was not proven uniform across the material
The surface reading was probably sufficient, and the later humidity increase mainly reflects normal sensor equilibration in the sealed sample
The humidity rebound most likely reflects cultivar-specific aroma compounds altering the reading after the material was sealed
Elapsed drying time should be weighted more heavily than the representative sample because surface texture is the more direct endpoint measure
rationale: Outer tissue can dry faster than the interior. Moisture rebound during stabilization indicates redistribution and can reveal that a drying endpoint was incomplete or uneven.
